newsitem.title: USA: Westmoreland says can't pay retiree benefits.
newsitem.headline: Westmoreland says can't pay retiree benefits.

text.p: Westmoreland Coal Co said Wednesday it is unable to pay for medical expenses of retirees who retired before October 1, 1994, because of a dispute with the United Mine Workers of America union.

The company said it has been unable to reach a longterm settlement with the union's Combined Benefit Fund, the 1992 UMWA Benefit Plan and the 1974 Pension Plan to resolve certain obligations to those entities.

Westmoreland said the Combined Benefit Fund has refused to release $2.7 million the company had placed in escrow, preventing the company from paying the medical expenses of retirees covered under the 1992 Benefit Plan.
As a result, the company said it is unable to reimburse Healthsource Provident for $1.8 million in claims, and Healthsource has suspended payment of any new claims.
The company said the 1992 Benefit Plan is now responsible for the medical expenses of retirees.

"The company does not have the cash or the income to continue paying the benefits," Westmoreland said. "The money it can raise by selling its remaining assets is not adequate to pay anything close to its remaining retiree health obligations." The 1992 plan was created by Congress to provide benefits for United Mine Workers of America retirees who retired before October 1, 1994, and whose companies were no longer able to provide those benefits.
There are about 1,200 Westmoreland retirees covered by the 1992 plan. Westmoreland said it expects to continue paying claims for beneficiaries under its other health plans.
